title: Covariant phase space and boundary ambiguities

items.title: Covariant field families and variations
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold and let $\pi:E\to M$ be a smooth fibre
bundle. A **field configuration** is a smooth section $\phi:M\to E$, so
$\pi\circ\phi=\operatorname{id}_M$. For a finite-dimensional smooth manifold
$P$, a **smooth field family** is a smooth map
$\Phi:P\times M\to E$ with $\pi(\Phi(p,x))=x$ for all $(p,x)$; it gives
configurations $\phi_p(x)=\Phi(p,x)$. For $u\in T_pP$, the **variation**
$\delta_u\phi_p$ at $x$ is the tangent vector
$d(r\mapsto\Phi(c(r),x))|_{r=0}$, where $c(0)=p$ and $c'(0)=u$. In a local
fibre chart this is the ordinary derivative of the field components with
respect to the parameter. For commuting parameter coordinates $s_1,s_2$,
$\delta_i\phi=\partial_{s_i}\phi$ and
$\delta_1\delta_2\phi=\delta_2\delta_1\phi$.

references.title: Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1, Field fibration and symplectic structure
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §2.2
Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §§2–3

items.title: Closed differential forms are exact on star-shaped coordinate domains
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and star-shaped with
respect to $a\in U$, and let $\alpha\in\Omega^k(U)$ be a smooth closed
differential form with $1\le k\le n$. Define

$$(K\alpha)_x(v_1,\ldots,v_{k-1}) :=\int_0^1 t^{k-1} \alpha_{a+t(x-a)}(x-a,v_1,\ldots,v_{k-1})\,dt .$$

Then $K\alpha$ is a smooth $(k-1)$-form on $U$ and $d(K\alpha)=\alpha$.

references.title: Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.3
Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §4

items.title: Differentiation of a smooth family of finite-chain integrals
items.design_state: Step 1 local analytic prerequisite developed from the exact finite-chain integration and Jordan Riemann definitions
items.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, let $M$ be an oriented smooth
four-manifold, and let $\Sigma$ be a fixed finite oriented smooth singular
three-chain in $M$. Let $\alpha_p$ be a smooth parameter-dependent
spacetime three-form, and assume that for every simplex in $\Sigma$ its
pullback coefficient is jointly smooth in the parameter coordinates and the
standard simplex coordinates. Define
$$I(p):=\int_\Sigma\alpha_p.$$
Then $I$ is smooth and, for every $v\in T_pP$,
$$d_PI_p(v)=\int_\Sigma d_P\alpha_p(v).$$

references.title: Peter S. Park, Proof of de Rham's Theorem
references.locator: Indirect source via the actually used local def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes and def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex: finite chains and simplex pullback integrals. The compact-parameter differentiation lemma is reconstructed locally, not attributed to this source.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis, Jordan Measurable Sets
references.locator: Indirect source via the actually used local def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set: zero-extension convention on compact simplex domains. Parameter differentiation and its uniform estimate are proved here.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis, Section 5.3: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

items.title: Covariant presymplectic current
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth four-manifold and let $\phi$ be a field
configuration in a specified smooth field bundle. A **local Lagrangian
four-form** $\mathcal L(\phi)$ is a smooth four-form whose coordinate
coefficients depend smoothly on the field components and finitely many
spacetime derivatives at each point. A **chosen first-variation
decomposition** consists of a linear Euler functional $E_\phi[\eta]$ with
values in four-forms and a three-form $\theta(\phi;\eta)$, each linear in the
field variation $\eta$ and its derivatives, such that every smooth
one-parameter field family satisfies

$$\delta\mathcal L=E_\phi[\delta\phi]+d_M\theta(\phi;\delta\phi).$$

The choice is part of the data; it is not asserted to be unique. In a
parameter family, $\delta_iE_\phi$ means the derivative of the coefficients
of $E_\phi$ with its variation input held fixed. Thus the total derivative of
$E_{\phi(p)}[\eta(p)]$ is
$(\delta_iE_\phi)[\eta]+E_\phi[\delta_i\eta]$. For a smooth
finite-dimensional field family with parameter exterior derivative $d_P$,
the one-form $\Theta$ on parameter space with values in spacetime three-forms
is $\Theta_p(v)=\theta(\phi_p;\delta_v\phi_p)$. Define the **covariant
presymplectic current** by $\omega:=-d_P\Theta$. For commuting parameter
coordinates $s_1,s_2$ this is

$$\omega(\delta_1\phi,\delta_2\phi) =\delta_2\theta(\phi;\delta_1\phi) -\delta_1\theta(\phi;\delta_2\phi).$$

For a finite oriented smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, define the
integrated two-form by
$\Omega_\Sigma(\delta_1\phi,\delta_2\phi)=\int_\Sigma\omega$.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3, equations (40)–(47)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.3

items.title: Variation identity for the presymplectic current
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Use the chosen first-variation decomposition and its Iyer–Wald current
ordering. For a smooth two-parameter family with commuting variations
$\delta_1,\delta_2$,

$$d_M\omega(\delta_1\phi,\delta_2\phi) =(\delta_1E_\phi)[\delta_2\phi]-(\delta_2E_\phi)[\delta_1\phi].$$

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3, equation (44)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §2.2, equation (2.25)

items.title: Closedness of the integrated presymplectic form on smooth field families
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
For a smooth finite-dimensional family of field configurations, let $\Theta$
be the parameter-space one-form with values in spacetime three-forms from the
chosen variational decomposition. For every finite oriented
smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, the integrated two-form
$\Omega_\Sigma=\int_\Sigma(-d_P\Theta)$ is closed on the parameter space:
$d_P\Omega_\Sigma=0$. This is a field-space identity and requires no
equations of motion. If a smooth solution family is specified, its restricted
form is also closed.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3, equations (44)–(45)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §2.2, equations (2.23)–(2.27)

items.title: On-shell closure and finite-region symplectic flux
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal L$ have a chosen first-variation decomposition with Euler
functional $E_\phi$. If $E_\phi=0$ and both variations satisfy the
linearized equations, so $\delta_iE_\phi=0$, then $d_M\omega=0$. For a finite
oriented smooth singular four-chain $C$ with
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, where the $\Sigma_i$ are oriented
three-chains and $B$ is the remaining oriented boundary chain,

$$\Omega_{\Sigma_2}-\Omega_{\Sigma_1}=-\int_B\omega.$$

Thus on-shell closure alone gives independence between cuts only when the
side flux vanishes.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3, equations (44)–(47)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §2.2, equation (2.25)

items.title: Potential ambiguity changes the current by a corner term
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
For a fixed smooth two-parameter family of commuting variations, replace the
Lagrangian and its selected potential by

$$\mathcal L'=\mathcal L+d_M\mu,\qquad \theta'(\phi;\delta\phi) =\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)+\delta\mu(\phi;\delta\phi) +d_MY(\phi;\delta\phi),$$

where $\mu$ is a local spacetime three-form and $Y$ is a local spacetime
two-form linear in the variation. Then

$$\omega'-\omega =d_M\bigl(\delta_2Y(\delta_1\phi)-\delta_1Y(\delta_2\phi)\bigr).$$

Consequently, for a finite oriented smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$,
the integrated form changes by the integral of this two-form over
$\partial\Sigma$.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3, equations (40)–(47)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.3, Some residual ambiguities
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.3

items.title: Diffeomorphism Noether current identity and local charge
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal L$ be a local Lagrangian four-form on an oriented smooth
four-manifold, with a chosen first-variation decomposition
$\delta\mathcal L=E_\phi[\delta\phi]+d_M\theta(\phi;\delta\phi)$. Let
$\xi$ be a smooth spacetime vector field that has a local flow acting on the
fields, and assume the Lagrangian is diffeomorphism covariant, meaning
$\delta_\xi\mathcal L=\mathcal L_\xi\mathcal L$ for
$\delta_\xi\phi=\mathcal L_\xi\phi$. Define the Noether current three-form

$$J_\xi:=\theta(\phi;\mathcal L_\xi\phi)-\iota_\xi\mathcal L .$$

Then

$$d_MJ_\xi=-E_\phi[\mathcal L_\xi\phi].$$

Thus $J_\xi$ is closed on solutions. On every star-shaped coordinate
neighborhood $U$, a solution has a local two-form $Q_\xi$ with
$J_\xi|_U=d_MQ_\xi$.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §4, equations (49)–(51)
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.3
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.3–2.4

items.title: Admissible presymplectic reduction and Hamiltonian generators
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a specified finite-dimensional smooth solution manifold
with specified admissible variations and boundary conditions, and let
$\Omega$ be a smooth closed two-form on $\mathcal S$, obtained by restricting
an integrated form $\Omega_\Sigma$ from the chosen covariant variation data.
The pair $(\mathcal S,\Omega)$ is **presymplectic** when $\Omega$ is allowed
to be degenerate. At $p\in\mathcal S$, its pointwise null space is
$$\ker\Omega_p:=\{v\in T_p\mathcal S:\Omega_p(v,w)=0 \text{ for every }w\in T_p\mathcal S\}.$$
A **presymplectic reduction** is defined here only when there is a specified
smooth Hausdorff manifold $\mathcal R$ and a surjective submersion
$q:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$ with connected fibers such that
$$\ker(dq_p)=\ker\Omega_p\qquad(p\in\mathcal S),$$
where $\ker(dq_p)$ consists of tangent vectors mapped to zero by the
differential. This condition makes the quotient fibers exactly the connected
directions annihilated by $\Omega$. The reduction further requires a smooth
closed nondegenerate two-form $\bar\Omega$ on $\mathcal R$ satisfying
$q^*\bar\Omega=\Omega$. For a smooth vector field $X$ and smooth function
$H$ on a specified phase space, the Hamiltonian convention is
$\iota_X\Omega=dH$.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §§1.3–1.4
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §2

items.title: Integrability of a covariant surface-charge variation
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal S,\Omega)$ be a specified smooth presymplectic solution space
and let $X_\xi$ be an admissible vector field generated by a specified
diffeomorphism parameter $\xi$ that preserves the boundary conditions. Define
the **charge-variation one-form**
$\alpha_\xi:=\iota_{X_\xi}\Omega$ on $\mathcal S$. It is **integrable on
$\mathcal S$** when there is a globally defined smooth function
$H_\xi:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R$ with $d_{\mathcal S}H_\xi=\alpha_\xi$; this
is the convention $\iota_{X_\xi}\Omega=d_{\mathcal S}H_\xi$. When a
finite-dimensional smooth parameter family is specified, a closed pullback
of $\alpha_\xi$ has local primitives on star-shaped coordinate patches;
global integrability on $\mathcal S$ is the stronger exactness condition.

references.title: Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.4.2, Integrability condition
Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.3–2.4

title: Covariant phase space and boundary ambiguities — Examples

items.title: Scalar-field potential and Cauchy-data pairing
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb T^3$ with periodic spatial coordinates
$(x,y,z)$ of period one, orientation
$dt\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, and flat metric
$g=-dt^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$. Write
$\mathrm{vol}=dt\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$. For one-forms, define the
Hodge map by
$$*dt=-dx\wedge dy\wedge dz,\quad *dx=-dt\wedge dy\wedge dz,\quad *dy=dt\wedge dx\wedge dz,\quad *dz=-dt\wedge dx\wedge dy,$$
and extend it linearly with smooth coefficients. Let
$\psi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, let $\mu\ge0$ be a fixed real parameter,
and take
$$\mathcal L=-\frac12d\psi\wedge *d\psi-\frac12\mu^2\psi^2\mathrm{vol}.$$
All objects here are mathematical; no physical units or empirical
interpretation are assigned. At the base solution $\psi=0$, take smooth
commuting variations satisfying
$(-\partial_t^2+\Delta-\mu^2)\delta_i\psi=0$. The chosen potential and
current are
$$\theta(\psi;\delta\psi)=-\delta\psi*d\psi,\qquad \omega(\delta_1,\delta_2) =\delta_2\psi*d\delta_1\psi-\delta_1\psi*d\delta_2\psi.$$
On the oriented cut $\Sigma_t=\{t\}\times\mathbb T^3$, with finite smooth
singular cycle obtained by triangulating the unit cube, the integrated form is
$$\Omega_{\Sigma_t}(\delta_1,\delta_2) =\int_{[0,1]^3} \bigl(\delta_1\psi\,\partial_t\delta_2\psi -\delta_2\psi\,\partial_t\delta_1\psi\bigr)\,dx\,dy\,dz.$$
With coordinate Lagrangian density
$\frac12(\partial_t\psi)^2-\frac12|\nabla\psi|^2-\frac12\mu^2\psi^2$,
the canonical momentum density is $\pi=\partial_t\psi$, so this is the
canonical Cauchy-data pairing.

references.title: Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §3.2, Two-derivative scalar field
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1
Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3

items.title: Closed bulk current with nonzero boundary flux
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned general-relativity covariant phase-space design
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ with coordinates $(t,x,y,z)$, orientation
$dt\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, and flat metric
$-dt^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$. For one-forms use
$$*dt=-dx\wedge dy\wedge dz,\qquad *dx=-dt\wedge dy\wedge dz,\qquad *dy=dt\wedge dx\wedge dz,\qquad *dz=-dt\wedge dx\wedge dy.$$
Let $\psi=0$ be the background of the massless scalar Lagrangian
$\mathcal L=-\tfrac12d\psi\wedge*d\psi$, with selected potential
$\theta(\psi;\delta\psi)=-\delta\psi*d\psi$ and current
$\omega(\delta_1,\delta_2)
=\delta_2\psi*d\delta_1\psi-\delta_1\psi*d\delta_2\psi$.
Take linearized solutions $\delta_1\psi=t^2+x^2$ and $\delta_2\psi=t$.
For $0<t_1<t_2$ and $L>0$,
let $C=[t_1,t_2]\times[0,L]\times[0,1]\times[0,1]$, with its oriented
finite smooth singular chain given by the standard coordinate-order
triangulation into $24$ four-simplices. Let $\Sigma_t$ be its lower or upper
spatial cut, as appropriate. Then the bulk current is closed, but
$$\Omega_{\Sigma_{t_2}}-\Omega_{\Sigma_{t_1}} =-L(t_2^2-t_1^2)\ne0.$$
The oriented side flux is $L(t_2^2-t_1^2)$, so the finite-region balance is
$\Omega_{\Sigma_{t_2}}-\Omega_{\Sigma_{t_1}}=-\int_B\omega$. The box is
compact; the example uses no asymptotic region or falloff premise.

references.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, §3
Geoffrey Compère and Adrien Fiorucci, Advanced Lectures on General Relativity, §1.3.1
Daniel Harlow and Jie-qiang Wu, Covariant phase space with boundaries, §§2.2–2.4
